discovery: Dynamical symmetries and supersymmetry in atomic nuclei: the interacting boson model
motivation: Francesco Iachello, with the late Akito Arima, created the interacting boson model, which describes collective states of complex nuclei through the algebra U(6). Its three dynamical symmetries, U(5), SU(3) and O(6), turned seemingly intractable many-body spectra into analytically solvable limits. These limits predicted energies, electromagnetic transitions and selection rules that experiments across the nuclear chart then confirmed. Iachello went on to propose dynamical supersymmetry linking even-even, odd-mass and odd-odd nuclei. High-resolution spectroscopy of the Au-Pt quartet in 1999 confirmed this prediction and gave the first experimental realization of supersymmetry in physics. His algebraic framework also introduced quantum shape phase transitions with critical-point symmetries (E(5), X(5)) and was carried over to molecular vibron spectra and hadrons. The work is a rare case of abstract symmetry giving precise, falsifiable predictions for strongly interacting quantum systems, and it remains a paradigm across physics.
